question.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(2,1,2)$, $B(3,3,3)$, $C(-2,-1,3)$, and $D(4,1,4).$

current_example.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(3,-1,2),$ $B(2,1,1),$ $C(-1,2,1),$ and $D(4,4,2).$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-i+2j-k \\  & =⟨-1,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+2j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-4i+3j-k \\  & =⟨-4,3,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(4i+4j+2k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =i+5j \\  & =⟨1,5,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3\cdot 0-5\cdot (-1))-2((-4)\cdot 0-1\cdot (-1))-((-4)\cdot 5-1\cdot 3) \\  & =-5-2+23 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is

$$
V=|16|=16.
$$
